intro: Words for «maybe»: the expression and your degree of certainty influence the mood.
p.quizá.consejo: It is also written «quizás». It takes indicative or subjunctive, depending on your certainty.
p.tal vez.consejo: It is two words. It works like «quizá»: «tal vez venga» or «tal vez viene».
p.puede que.consejo: Always with the subjunctive: «puede que nieve». «Puede» does not change here.
p.es probable que.consejo: It asks for the subjunctive: «es probable que llueva». «Probable» is the opposite of «improbable».
p.a lo mejor.consejo: Very common in speech. Unlike «quizá», it almost always takes the indicative: «a lo mejor viene».
p.igual.consejo: In Spain you hear it a lot: «igual llueve». It takes the indicative. It is very informal.
p.seguro que.consejo: Almost total certainty: indicative. «Seguro que vienes» is almost a statement.
p.supongo que.consejo: It takes the indicative: «supongo que tienes frío». It is less certain than «sé que».
p.no sé si.consejo: «Si» without an accent means «whether». With an accent, «sí», it is «yes». It takes the indicative.
p.probablemente.consejo: It is formed from «probable» + «-mente». It allows indicative or subjunctive.
p.seguramente.consejo: It does not mean «with total certainty»: it is closer to «probably».
p.sierra.consejo: The rr in the middle sounds strong: «SYE-rra». It is also a tool, a saw.
p.nevar.consejo: It changes e to ie: «nieva», «nieve». It only has the «él / ella» form.
p.me quedo.consejo: It comes from «quedarse». With «a lo mejor» it goes in the indicative: «a lo mejor me quedo».
b1.texto:
There are three groups of expressions:

- Almost always **indicative**: **a lo mejor**, **igual**, **seguro que**, **supongo que**. Example: **a lo mejor me quedo** at home.
- Always **subjunctive**: **puede que**, **es posible que**, **es probable que**. Example: **puede que nieve**.
- **Both moods**: **quizá(s)**, **tal vez**, **probablemente**, **seguramente**. Example: **quizá viene** or **quizá venga**.

With the last group, the subjunctive sounds more doubtful and the indicative more certain.

**No sé si** takes the indicative in Spain: **no sé si viene**. Without an accent, **si** means «whether»; with an accent, **sí** is «yes».
b2.f0.texto: Are you coming to the mountains on Saturday?
b2.f1.texto: I don't know if I can.
b2.f3.texto: It may snow in the mountains.
b2.f4.texto: It is likely to be very cold.
b2.f5.texto: Then maybe I will stay at home.
b2.f6.texto: I am sure you will come in the end.
b2.f7.texto: Perhaps I will bring my big coat.
b4.texto:
Follow this guide:

- **Indicative**: a lo mejor · igual · seguro que · supongo que · no sé si.
- **Subjunctive**: puede que · es posible que · es probable que.
- **Both moods**: quizá(s) · tal vez · probablemente · posiblemente · seguramente.

With the third group, choose according to how **sure** you are: if you think it is very likely, indicative (**quizá viene**); if you doubt more, subjunctive (**quizá venga**).

If you put the adverb **after** the verb, it is always indicative: viene, **quizá**.
b5.f0.texto: The mountains wake up wrapped in a white, still mist.
b5.f1.texto: The black pines peep out between the clouds like giant needles.
b5.f2.texto: An icy wind comes down the slope and whistles between the rocks.
b5.f3.texto: The first snowflakes fall slowly onto the path.
b5.f4.texto: Lucía watches them with a red nose and a girl's smile.
b5.f5.texto: Near the shelter, a column of smoke rises from the chimney.
b5.f6.texto: Inside it smells of firewood and hot soup.
b5.f7.texto: Pablo shakes the snow off his boots by the door.
b5.f8.texto: The warden offers them a thick blanket and two cups of broth.
b5.f9.texto: Through the window the two of them look at the white, silent valley.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Puede que» always goes with the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Nieva» is indicative; after «puede que» it does not fit.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Nevará» is future; here you need the subjunctive.
b6.pregunta: Snow is only a possibility. What is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «A lo mejor» almost always takes the indicative.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes! «Tal vez» allows both, depending on your certainty.
b7.pregunta: Which one allows both indicative and subjunctive?
b8.frase: A lo mejor me ____ en casa.
b8.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «A lo mejor» takes the indicative.
b8.o1.refuerzo: «Quede» is subjunctive; with «a lo mejor» it is not used.
b8.o2.refuerzo: A conjugated, reflexive verb is needed.
b8.pregunta: «A lo mejor» asks for the indicative. What is missing?
b9.frase: Quizá tenga que trabajar el sábado
b9.traduccion: Maybe I have to work on Saturday
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Seguro que» is almost a statement.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Quizá» with the subjunctive leaves a lot of doubt.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Maybe I'll stay at home».
b12.o0.refuerzo: In Spain, «no sé si» takes the indicative, not the subjunctive.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Here a conjugated verb is needed.
b12.pregunta: You don't know if Pablo is coming. What is missing?
p.amanece.consejo: From «amanecer», the day begins. The «c» before «e» sounds like «th».
p.envuelta.consejo: From «envolver», to wrap. It describes a feminine noun, so it ends in -a.
p.asoman.consejo: From «asomarse», to show yourself little by little. The «s» is soft and clear.
p.agujas.consejo: Thin pointed leaves of pine trees. «Aguja» is feminine: «la aguja».
p.ladera.consejo: The sloping side of a mountain. Its «d» stays soft, as in «la-DE-ra».
p.silba.consejo: From «silbar», to whistle. A wind can whistle too, not only people.
p.copos.consejo: Small light pieces of snow. «Copo» is masculine: «el copo».
p.refugio.consejo: A simple place to be safe from weather. The «g» before «i» sounds like «h».
p.columna.consejo: Something tall and straight, like smoke rising up. It is feminine: «la columna».
p.leña.consejo: Wood for the fire. The «ñ» sounds like «ny».
p.caldo.consejo: A warm liquid cooked from meat or vegetables. Its «c» is hard: «KAL-do».
p.quedo.consejo: Without noise or movement. The «qu» sounds like «k».
